podcast.body: Released in 1989, this album made it onto the Billboard charts but was considered "a little too much too soon for prime time." It preceded their breakthrough album, "Badmotorfinger," which would establish them as part of the grunge "holy trinity." "Their previous album, Louder Than Love in 1989, did okay, at least it made it onto the Billboard charts, but it was a little too much too soon for prime time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album was released after Soundgarden signed to a major label. However, at the time *Singles* was being filmed in early 1991, the album had not yet "registered" outside of the metal community, indicating that the Seattle grunge scene was still largely unknown to the broader public. "Yes, Soundgarden had signed to a major label and had released their louder than love album, but outside the metal community, it didn't really register."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This was Soundgarden's second album and their debut on major label A&M Records. It achieved a milestone by becoming the first Grunge LP to enter the Billboard album chart, reaching number 108 in early 1990. At this time, the band was still marketed as metal, and the Seattle scene had not yet become a mainstream phenomenon. "Louder Than Love, became the first Grunge LP to make the Billboard album chart, where it reached number 108 in early 1990."
